STANDARD: The Healthcare Organisation ensures patients are provided with safe, high- quality inpatient and outpatient care throughout the care delivery process. They should do this from the time that the patient enters the healthcare organisation or service through to when the patient is discharged or transferred to another health facility-service; and during any ongoing care they provide after discharge.
The Healthcare Organisation should implement evidence-based practice and a have a process for assessing the appropriateness and effectiveness of care and services, and the settings they are delivered in.
Standard 17 National Health Service Standards (NHSS) Vol. 2 (2nd Edition) National Quality Standard

Mortuary services shall be provided within the Facility. The Mortuary Services shall include but are not limited to the provision of;
Body reception
Body services
Body preparation/release area
Body Area for body viewing
Bereavement /Counselling room
Post-mortem suite (where available)
The Mortuary Services are organised and administered to provide quality services appropriate to the level of mortuary services provided by the Facility.

The Vision, Mission of the Facility are accessible. The Goals of the Mortuary Services suit its scope and are clearly documented. It should reflect the aspirations of the service and the needs of the community.
The Mission, Vision and Goals of the Organisation are visible, endorsed and dated.
There is an endorsed and dated department organisational chart with lines of functions and reporting relationships.
Relevant policies and guidelines are available in the department, i.e., National Health Plan, National Health Service Standards, etc.)

Evidence of fee structure (if fees are collected).
There is a mechanism to ensure effective interaction between the Officer in Charge (OIC) and the Organisation’s Governing Body and Senior Management.

Letter of appointment and terms of reference in other hospital committees.

Regular staff meetings are held between the Officer Head of Service and staff with sufficient regularity to discuss issues pertaining to the Mortuary Services. These meetings are minuted and communicated to all staff.
Meeting minutes are available, disseminated and acknowledged by staff.

Frequency of meetings are as scheduled.
Discussions and resolutions are implemented. (problems not solved are brought forward to the next meeting till resolved).

The statistics and records from (a) to (f) are available.
The Mortuary Services shall be supervised by a suitably qualified, trained and competent practitioner and assisted by relevant categories of staff.

The Officer in Charge and staff of the Mortuary Services shall be individuals qualified by education, training, experience and certification to meet the demands of the various positions and to achieve the objectives of the services.
There is evidence that the staff have some training or experience in the processes governing the mortuary.

Administrative and clinical job scope
There are dated and specific job descriptions for each staff that include (a) to (d).

The scope of work in the job description aligns with the training, skill and experience of the staff (credentialling).

Observation that cadres of staff are working according to their job description and job scope.

Training calendar includes in-house/ external courses/ workshops/ conferences.

Staff receive evaluation of their performance at the completion of the probationary period and annually thereafter, or as defined by the Organisation.

There is a structured orientation programme for all Mortuary Services staff;

Lines of authority and areas of responsibility.

There are written and dated policies for all activities of the Mortuary Services. These policies reflect current standards, relevant regulations and statutory requirements. These policies and procedures, terms of reference, by laws, rules and regulations state how the Mortuary Services staff regulate themselves and their operational practice.
There are written policies and procedures for the Mortuary Services which are consistent with the overall policies of the Facility, regulatory requirements and current standard practices.
Evidence of documented policies and procedures for the service.
The policies and procedures are endorsed and dated.
There is a periodic review at least once in three years.
Copies of policies, by laws, regulations and relevant acts are accessible on site for staff reference.
Policies and procedures are developed by a committee in collaboration with staff and with other departments if needed.
Minutes of committee meetings on development and revision on policies and procedures.

Documented policies and procedures that address (a) to (m).

There is evidence of compliance to the policies and procedures (staff interview, observation, review of patient complaints, results of audits).

There are written instructions for the proper handling of the specimens as required by law which include collection, labelling, sealing, packaging, transport of specimens, dispatch/handing over to relevant authority. 
These instructions are readily accessible to the staff. The preservation of chain of evidence shall be maintained throughout the process of specimen handling.
There are Standard Operating Procedures /work instructions on how to handle specimens.

All specimens and evidences taken from the deceased.

All movement of records or reports out of the forensic services.
Complete records and documentation of body management including (a) to (e).

There are written safety procedures and manuals on hazards and safety precautions specific to the Mortuary Services. All staff shall practice Standard Precautions and Safety Guidelines.
Standard Operating Procedures and manuals on safety procedures are available.

The Officer in Charge of Mortuary Services shall ensure adequate facilities and equipment for the safe and efficient provision of Mortuary Services taking into consideration the scope of services and potentially hazardous circumstances of the Mortuary Services. This shall comply with relevant regulations and statutory requirements.

The mortuary shall be accessible from an outside entrance and following a designated route of the Facility. Appropriate transport for transferring bodies to the mortuary that to ensure dignity and respect is accorded to the deceased.
Mortuary is accessible from an outside entrance to the Facility.
Conveyance of body to the Mortuary is via a designated route and entrance.
Proper covered body trolley and appropriate transport are available to transfer the body

There are designated areas for body cleansing/preparation, body viewing, bereavement, performing cultural rites and release of bodies.

The Head of the Mortuary Services shall ensure that the staff are trained and complete incident reports which are promptly reported, investigated, discussed by the staff with learning objectives.
Incidents reported have had Root Cause Analysis done and action taken within the agreed time frame to prevent recurrence.

Method/SOP on Incident reporting
Register of incidents
Involved staff given feedback about the incident report
Acknowledgment by Head of Mortuary Service and Director of Curative Services.
Remedial action is taken when appropriate
